Why Guests Love Adding Tour Photos

Shark diving is one of those experiences that’s hard to fully appreciate until you see the photos afterward. When the conditions come together, shark diving can produce some truly surreal images—the kind you look at later and think, “I actually did that.” They become something you share, revisit, and keep long after the trip is over.

It’s not something everyone needs to add—but if great photos matter to you, this may be something you won't want to miss.

  • 40-60+ High Quality Photos
    You get an extensive collection of high resolution, professional photos.
  • High-end Equipment
    Our photographers use high-end underwater photography equipment including high-end camera bodies, lenses, and underwater housing.
  • Expert Shark Divers & Safety Professionals
    Our photographers are certified water safety professionals and expert shark divers, so they can get you incredible shots safely.
  • One-on-One Experience
    Our guests find that diving one-on-one with a photographer who understands shark behavior, freediving, and how to position for incredible shots results in a more premium experience overall.

Shark Diving Tour

Frequently Asked Questions

Tour Safety

Every tour includes a safety briefing before entering the water, and experienced safety divers stay with guests throughout the swim. The team closely watches shark behavior, ocean conditions, and the group so guests can focus on enjoying the experience.

These are wild animals in the open ocean, so the sharks are always treated with respect and safety comes first.

Absolutely. It’s completely normal to feel nervous before getting into the open ocean with sharks—especially if it’s your first time.

For many guests, that nervousness goes away once they’re in the water and see the sharks for themselves. What initially feels intimidating is often replaced by an almost overwhelming excitement, curiosity, and wonder.

The crew will explain what to expect before entering the water and will be there with you throughout the experience, so you can take things at your own pace and get comfortable.

You do not need to be a strong swimmer or have diving experience. You can enjoy the entire shark encounter snorkeling at the surface, and the crew will stay with you and assist throughout the experience.

Guests who are comfortable freediving may choose to dive below the surface, but that is completely optional.

No. This is a snorkeling and freediving experience, not a scuba dive. No scuba certification is required, and snorkel equipment is provided.

The minimum age is 5 years old with an accompanying adult, and no previous shark-diving, freediving, or scuba experience is required.

The crew continuously evaluates shark behavior, visibility, ocean conditions, and each guest’s comfort level throughout the experience. If conditions aren’t appropriate for a particular guest to enter the water, the crew will always put safety first.

Guests with serious health conditions should consult their physician before participating.

Seasickness can happen, especially for guests who are sensitive to boat motion, and being on a small boat in the open ocean can cause seasickness even for people who don’t normally think of themselves as prone to it.

If you’re sensitive to motion or think there’s a chance you may get seasick, the best thing you can do is prepare ahead of time. Motion-sickness medications and other preventative strategies are generally most effective when used before symptoms begin, so it’s worth looking into your options before the day of your tour.

Getting a good night’s sleep, staying hydrated, avoiding alcohol the night before, and eating appropriately before the trip can also help.

It’s also a good idea to familiarize yourself with what to do if you start feeling seasick while you’re on the boat. A little preparation can make a big difference in how much you enjoy the experience.

Read our complete guide to preventing and managing seasickness before your tour: Managing Seasickness

The Shark Diving Experience

The goal is a more personal and immersive shark-diving experience rather than simply watching sharks from a distance.

Tours are limited to a maximum of six guests, and the team includes highly experienced shark divers, divemasters, freedivers, captains, marine professionals, and underwater photographers who spend significant time working with sharks in the open ocean.

There is no fixed distance because every encounter is different and the sharks choose how they move through the water.

Sharks often come quite close. When conditions and shark behavior allow, the team gives guests the freedom to have a more immersive encounter rather than simply observing from one position. If you would rather keep more distance, that is completely fine too.

Common encounters can include Galapagos sharks, tiger sharks, hammerheads, and other pelagic shark species found around Oʻahu.

The exact animals you encounter vary because these are wild sharks in their natural environment.

Sharks are wild animals, so wildlife encounters can never be guaranteed.

Every day in the ocean is different, and shark activity can vary with conditions. That unpredictability is also part of what makes seeing them in their natural environment so special.

Your tour begins at Haleʻiwa Harbor, where you’ll meet the crew and get settled on the boat. Plan to arrive at least 15 minutes before your scheduled departure so there’s plenty of time to check in and get ready.

From the harbor, it’s roughly a 15–30 minute boat ride to the shark diving site, about three miles offshore. Along the way, you’ll get great views of Oʻahu’s North Shore and may spot wildlife such as sea turtles, dolphins, flying fish, or even surfers near the harbor depending on the season and conditions.

During the ride out, your safety diver will go over what to expect in the water, explain the equipment and safety procedures, talk about the sharks and surrounding marine environment, and answer any questions you have. It’s also a chance to get to know the crew and, if you’ve booked the photo package, your photographer.

When you reach the dive site, a safety diver enters the water first to evaluate the conditions and shark activity. Once everything looks good, you’ll put on your snorkel gear and enter the water with the crew.

Most guests spend around 45 minutes in the water, although the exact amount of dive time can vary with conditions. You’ll be able to snorkel at the surface, watch the sharks move through the water, and simply take in the experience. Guests who have booked photography can also work with the photographer on positioning, hand signals, and the kinds of shots they’d like to capture.

If you want to take a break, you can return to the boat and get back in the water afterward, as conditions and timing allow.

When the dive is finished, you’ll climb back aboard, dry off, change if you’d like, and get settled for the ride back to Haleʻiwa Harbor. The return trip is another chance to enjoy the North Shore from offshore and talk with the crew about the dive.

Once back at the harbor, you’ll gather your belongings and head out from there. The full experience is usually just under two hours from departure to return.

There is no restroom on the boat, so it’s a good idea to use a restroom before arriving at the harbor.

Six.

The smaller group gives guests more room, more direct access to the crew, and more opportunity to enjoy the sharks without spending the experience crowded among a large group of swimmers.

Approx. 2 hours. This includes the boat ride to and from the dive site, safety briefing, preparation, and time in the water.

Planning Your Tour

Your tour includes the approximately two-hour boat trip, safety briefing, experienced crew and safety divers, and the snorkel equipment needed for the dive.

Transportation to Haleiwa harbor from other parts of the island is not included.

Bring a valid photo ID, towel, reef-safe sunscreen, and a change of clothes if you’d like to be dry for the ride back.

A light jacket can also be useful because it may be windy on the boat. Sunglasses, a hat, and a waterproof camera such as a GoPro are welcome as well.

Snorkel gear is provided, so you do not need to bring your own unless you prefer to.

Wear swimwear that you’re comfortable snorkeling in.

You’ll be entering the open ocean directly from the boat, so choose something that stays secure and allows you to move comfortably in the water.

Tours depart from Haleiwa Harbor on Oʻahu’s North Shore.

Your booking confirmation should provide the exact meeting and check-in instructions for your tour.

Yes. Hawaii Adventure Diving offers a Non-Diver Ride Along option for guests who want to join the boat trip and experience the adventure without entering the water.

This can be a great option for couples, families, or groups where not everyone wants to shark dive.

Weather, Changes & Cancellation

Ocean conditions can change, and safety always takes priority.

The captain and crew evaluate conditions before and during every trip and determine whether the tour can be operated safely. If conditions affect your scheduled tour, the team will work with you on the available options.

Hawaii Adventure Diving offers free cancellation up to 48 hours before your scheduled tour.

Cancellations within 48 hours of the tour and no-shows are charged the full tour amount.
